title: Wildfire Smoke Forecast (Transparent) — United States (RRFS)
abstract:
Wildfire smoke drifting across the United States, forecast hour by hour. The colour shows how much smoke is in the air overhead — all of it, from the ground to the top of the sky, added up into a single column. Pale yellow is a thin haze; deep orange is thick smoke. Where the map shows through, the air is clear.

Smoke from a large fire does not stay put. It rises, catches the winds a few kilometres up, and can travel a continent away while the fire that made it burns on. That is why a clear day on the ground can still sit under a smoke plume.

An 84-hour hourly outlook on the NOAA Rapid Refresh Forecast System's 3 km CONUS domain. Frames are data-encoded: the brightness of each pixel carries the measured value, so hovering reports the smoke loading in kilograms per square metre rather than a colour.
